He decreased the distance, but on reaching the dressing room, Parker still had sufficient lead to keep his opponent at a respectable distance, and won the race in 4 min. 32 sec.—time which equals the Club record.

Parker, Penny and Cohen finished equal first, closely followed by Shaw, Williams and Verney. We were obviously much too strong for our University friends, who lacked the assistance of Etheridge; but, nevertheless, the sporting match was greatly enjoyed by all.

At this point, Highgate seemed to have the team race well in hand, with Shaw not far behind Tunbridge and Brazier. The "Bels" were ahead of Woodford, who had three men well up—Cotton, Goodall and Foster—but whose fourth man (then Alf.

The individual handicap was won by Evans of Highgate, Shaw of Queens Park H. was 2nd and Len Demmon 3rd.. Bernard Eglington, on his last days leave from Germany, took the prize for the first Belgrave member unplaced in the scratch events.

Dennis Merrett was most unlucky to come up against two hurdlers (Vine and Shaw) at the peak of their form and although his time of 24.7 secs. was a little slower than his Southern Championship record made a few weeks earlier, his performance was nevertheless of a very high standard.
